  "title": "matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)') returns false while other WCO signals report active",
  "body": "### Preflight Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.\n- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.\n- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.\n\n### Electron Version\n\n41.3.0\n\n### What operating system(s) are you using?\n\nOther Linux\n\n### Operating System Version\n\nReproduced on Nobara 43 (Fedora-based, KDE Plasma 6, kernel 6.19.10) under both X11 and Wayland sessions, and on Windows 11 (23H2) in a VM today.\n\n### What arch are you using?\n\nx64\n\n### Last Known Working Electron version\n\nNone within the currently-supported window. The same probe reproduces identically on 38.8.6 (Chromium 140), 39.8.9 (Chromium 142), 40.9.2 (Chromium 144), and 41.3.0 (Chromium 146) on Linux, and on 41.3.0 on Windows 11. Either this has always been wrong or it regressed before 38, which is EOL.\n\n### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?\n\nNo\n\n### Expected Behavior\n\nWhen a `BrowserWindow` is created with `frame: false`, `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, and a populated `titleBarOverlay` object, all four standard WCO entry points should agree:\n\n1. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` → `true`\n2. `windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()` → non-zero rect\n3. `env(titlebar-area-width / -height / -x / -y)` → populated CSS env values\n4. `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches` → `true`\n\nThe W3C [Window Controls Overlay explainer](https://github.com/WICG/window-controls-overlay/blob/main/explainer.md) and the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Controls_Overlay_API) both name the media query as the recommended CSS detection point.\n\n### Actual Behavior\n\nThree of four signals report WCO active. **Only `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` disagrees and returns `matches: false`.** The same mismatch reproduces on Linux and on Windows 11.\n\nProbe output, Electron 41.3.0, Linux (Wayland; X11 identical):\n\n```\nnavigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true\ngetTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 804 × 40\nenv(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 804px\nenv(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px\nmatchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false\n```\n\nProbe output, Electron 41.3.0, Windows 11:\n\n```\nnavigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true\ngetTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 763 × 40\nenv(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 763px\nenv(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px\nmatchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false\n```\n\nThe titlebar-area rect matches the configured `titleBarOverlay.height: 40` on both platforms, which confirms Chromium has applied WCO at the layout level. The CSS `env()` values share that source. But pages following the W3C-recommended detection pattern see WCO as inactive and skip the WCO-specific layout they would have rendered.\n\n### Testcase Gist URL\n\nhttps://gist.github.com/aaddrick/90a16bf22da070e07ff382c7a89ae3d8\n\n### Additional Information\n\n**Relationship to #51389.** I filed [#51389](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51389) earlier today framing this as Linux-specific. After source investigation and a Windows 11 reproduction, that framing was wrong. I withdrew #51389 and am refiling here with the corrected scope. The probe output, gist, and sibling repo are unchanged; only the platform list and the root-cause section are new.\n\n**Root cause.** Electron's `WebContents` (`shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.h:124-125`) inherits from `content::WebContentsDelegate` and overrides ~50 methods. It does not override `GetDisplayMode()`. A full grep of the tree confirms zero references to `display_mode` outside two unrelated header includes. Without an override, Chromium's default returns `blink::mojom::DisplayMode::kBrowser`, which gets baked into `WebPreferences::display_mode` in `RenderViewHostImpl::ComputeWebPreferences()` and shipped to Blink. The matchMedia evaluator for `(display-mode: …)` reads from there, so it always evaluates against `kBrowser` regardless of how the BrowserWindow was configured.\n\nThe other three signals work because they take a separate mojo path: `NativeWindow::NotifyLayoutWindowControlsOverlay()` → `BrowserWindow::UpdateWindowControlsOverlay()` (`electron_api_browser_window.cc:205`) → `web_contents()->UpdateWindowControlsOverlay(rect)`. That path never touches the `display_mode` web preference, so it stays at `kBrowser` and the four signals diverge.\n\n**Fix.** I have a 16-line patch on a local branch that overrides `GetDisplayMode()` on Electron's `WebContents` and routes the answer through the same `IsWindowControlsOverlayEnabled()` gate (`native_window.h:390-398`) the other three signals already use. Same input, same answer; the four signals agree by construction. The override also returns `kFullscreen` for fullscreen windows and `kStandalone` for frameless windows without titleBarOverlay, which matches Chromium's PWA semantics so existing `isStandalone()`-style checks (e.g., the one in microsoft/vscode#160696) keep working. With the patch applied on Linux, the probe table reads `matches: true` and all four signals agree. PR coming separately.\n\n**Sibling repo with the Chromium PWA companion test.** I published the same Electron Fiddle files alongside a Chromium-side PWA repro at https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch. The Electron repro lives at the repo root (mirrors the gist). The Chromium-side test is under [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa). Either source works.\n\n**AI disclosure** (per the Electron governance AI policy): I drafted the repro and this report with assistance from Anthropic's Opus 4.7 via Claude Code. I ran the repro locally on Electron 41.3.0 (Nobara 43 / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland) and on a Windows 11 VM, empirically verified the four-signal mismatch on both, and reviewed this body line-by-line before submission. I'm responsible for the contents and can answer follow-up questions.\n\n**How I ran into this.** It surfaced during [aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian#538](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/pull/538), packaging an Electron-based web app for Linux. The bundled web app uses `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` to decide whether to render its WCO-aware topbar. On Electron Linux that returns `false` even though WCO is active, so the topbar silently doesn't render. I assumed it was Linux-only because that's where I first saw it; the Windows VM repro disproved that.\n\n**Concrete impact.** Pages whose conditional WCO layout relies on the `@media (display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` rule render their non-WCO layout while WCO is active, which causes visual collisions with the overlay area on every Electron platform. Pages that detect via `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` work correctly. Most JS-side detection examples in the wild use one or both, and any that use only the `@media` route are silently broken.",
